Ravi: Quick follow-up on the service auth convo: propose we support 'artifact-locked' tokens (token is valid only when runtime proves it is running a specific artifact_sha). Pros/cons?
Jules: Pros: improves replay/clone safety. Also useful for attestation in regulated customers.
Marta: Cons: CI churn. If we lock to every build SHA, we'll have tokens minted every deploy. How do we avoid token explosion?
Ravi: Two knobs: 1) mint short TTL tokens at deploy-time and rotate automatically, 2) allow token to be issued against an artifact family tag (e.g., image:stable or model:v1) to reduce churn.
Jules: Family tag is nice. But then you lose some security guarantees. Maybe allow customers to choose enforcement level (strict|family|host-bound).
infra-bot: note: deploy service-api/2026-03-22 finished (sha=sha256:deadbeef)
Marta: Another important piece: scoping. Tokens still need project/org claims for billing, quotas, and RBAC. We should not conflate artifact binding with project scope. Keep both claims.
Nina: Agreed. Policy evaluation should be two step: verify token claims (project/org/role), then runtime check artifact claim matches environment. If either fails -> deny.
Ravi: What about long-running batch jobs that cross token TTL? Option: issue a job-session token exchanged from the short token (token-exchange endpoint) with limited extra TTL but pinned to artifact and job-id.
Jules: Need strong rules for exchange: require deploy-time signature proof (CI key) + token in-hand. Also make sure exchange is auditable and can be revoked.
Marta: Revocation model: maintain a short blacklist for artifact SHAs and token nonces, but rely mainly on TTL. Full revocation table at scale could be high cardinality; maybe we keep per-project revocation epochs instead.
Nina: For RBAC, we should extend policy language with artifact predicates: allow if artifact in allowlist OR artifact matches pattern. Keep this optional feature flag to start.
Ravi: UX/ops: Console should show tokens issued per-artifact, last-used, and ability to revoke artifact family. Also provide infra API to bulk-revoke tokens for a project.
Jules: Implementation approach: reuse existing token service; add optional artifact claim and a lightweight runtime hook that calls policy service to verify artifact predicate. No huge refactor required.
Marta: Action items: Ravi -> draft token-exchange flow + claim shape. Nina -> policy predicate extension spec. Jules -> incremental implementation plan (token service + runtime hook). I'll file an RFC appendix and link back.
Ravi: Thanks. I'll start the RFC addendum and include sample claim examples and a few diag sketches. :thumbsup:
